---
title: "Licensing & Copyright"
---

3 requirement(s) in this category.

### LIC-001 — Apache-2.0 copyright header on every file {#sec-lic-001}

**Mathlib + PhysLean** · Level **SHALL**

Every source file SHALL begin with a copyright header naming the year and author(s) and releasing the file under the Apache-2.0 license, e.g.

```
/-
Copyright (c) 2025 Your Name. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Your Name
-/
```

**Acceptance criteria**

- The file's first block is the copyright header.
- The header names the release year and all authors.
- The header cites the Apache-2.0 license and the LICENSE file.

**Rationale.** A uniform, machine-checkable license header keeps provenance and licensing unambiguous for every file in the library.

**Verify.** The style linter checks for a well-formed header (mathlib: lint-style; physlean: ./scripts/lint-style.sh).

**Source.** <http://physlib.io/getting-started>

---

### LIC-002 — Authors line format {#sec-lic-002}

**Mathlib** · Level **SHALL**

The header SHALL use `Authors:` even when there is a single author, SHALL separate all author names with commas (not the word `and` before the final author), and SHALL NOT end the author line with a period.

**Acceptance criteria**

- The line begins `Authors:`.
- Multiple authors are comma-separated with no `and`.
- There is no trailing period.

**Rationale.** A single fixed format lets tooling parse authorship reliably.

**Source.** <https://leanprover-community.github.io/contribute/style.html>

---

### LIC-003 — Contributions are Apache-2.0 licensed {#sec-lic-003}

**Mathlib + PhysLean** · Level **SHALL**

By contributing, the author SHALL release the contribution under the Apache-2.0 license, consistent with the project as a whole.

**Acceptance criteria**

- The contribution carries the Apache-2.0 header and introduces no incompatibly-licensed material.

**Rationale.** A single permissive license across the library avoids licensing fragmentation and legal ambiguity for downstream users.

**Source.** <http://physlib.io/get-involved>
